blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Tumor delineation is required for radiotherapy planning, yet automatic segmentation is limited by errors, predominantly false positives, that distort dose and increase editing time. The radiology report accompanies the scan and localizes disease at the suborgan level, but existing text-promptable models condition on short referring phrases, and most operate in 2D. We present RepConTUR, a single native-3D early-fusion multimodal model that conditions volumetric abdominal tumor segmentation on the narrative report. We extend AbdomenAtlas 3.0 to a suborgan-level promptable segmentation dataset and generate report-based VQA pairs, yielding four report-derived tasks on the same annotations: referring segmentation (RES), report-grounded segmentation (GSEG), report generation (RRG), and visual question answering (VQA). We train RepConTUR, comprising a 3D CT encoder, an early-fusion language model, and a native-3D segmentation module, jointly on the four tasks. Across liver, kidney and pancreas, RepConTUR attains the highest Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), instance-wise precision, and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and adding the report raises mean precision while leaving recall comparable. Against two vision-only specialists, nnU-Net and the report-supervised R-Super, RepConTUR attains the highest value on every in-domain metric for liver and pancreas and the highest mean DSC, recall, precision, and detection F1 over the four out-of-distribution public cohorts. Ablations indicate that conditioning on the narrative report raises detection F1 from 0.499 to 0.528 within the same model, that joint GSEG training raises RES F1 from 0.450 to 0.482, and that the native-3D segmentation module raises GSEG F1 from 0.139 to 0.528 over its 2D counterpart. Code is available at https://github.com/Oncosoft-Research/RepConTUR.

blocks.en:
Tumor delineation is a required step in radiotherapy planning, but manual
contouring is labor-intensive and shows large inter-observer variability [ 58 , 52 , 21 ] . Unlike diagnostic reading, radiotherapy target
contouring routinely combines the diagnostic scan with its radiology report, as the report
contains rich information about the tumor, including its anatomical location, size and
stage [ 29 , 7 , 20 , 1 ] . This makes the report a natural conditioning signal for automatic tumor
segmentation.

Vision-only deep learning models remain the standard approach to tumor segmentation, and their
accuracy is reported mainly by the volumetric Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), which
underrepresents instance-wise recall and precision [ 37 ] . On the LiTS
liver-tumor benchmark, the top method reports a tumor Dice of 0.702 0.702 , yet its instance-wise precision
is only 0.148 0.148 [ 6 ] . In
radiotherapy, instance-wise recall and precision are as clinically important as DSC. False positives in particular distort the
dose distribution and raise normal-tissue exposure and toxicity risk [ 44 ] , and these errors increase the editing time [ 57 ] .
A separate line of work uses the radiology report as training-time supervision to improve tumor
detection and segmentation. Report-derived tumor count and size penalize inconsistent predictions
through auxiliary losses [ 3 ] , reported location provides weak
labels [ 23 ] , and the report yields pseudo-labels [ 9 ] .
However, these models still segment from the image alone at inference time [ 64 ] , so the report cannot directly inform the prediction.

Text-guided segmentation models have achieved strong results on referring segmentation (RES)
and grounded segmentation (GSEG) [ 63 , 31 , 45 , 76 , 33 ] . Some works adopt a dual-encoder design that encodes the language prompt and the image
in separate branches and fuses them at the decoder [ 70 , 47 ] . On the other hand, multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based segmentation models fuse image and
text early and reason over both jointly within the language model [ 31 , 61 ] . Yet both are designed for
short target descriptions — class names or referring phrases — and do not exploit long-form
textual context. BiomedParse v2, for
example, conditions on an organ-level prompt (e.g., “tumor in liver CT”), which cannot indicate a
detailed intra-organ region and may not capture suborgan-level information [ 70 , 71 ] .
A report instead specifies suborgan location, which may help suppress false positives elsewhere in
the same organ [ 18 , 17 ] . Furthermore, existing MLLM-based medical segmentation models are also mostly
2D [ 61 ] , limiting their abilities to interpret report information that refers to 3D context [ 30 , 11 , 38 ] .

blocks.en:
We propose RepConTUR, an MLLM-based 3D report-conditioned tumor segmentation
model that grounds segmentation on the report to improve both segmentation accuracy and instance-wise
detection ( Fig. 1 ). Our contributions are threefold: • Report-conditioned segmentation. We condition segmentation on a suborgan-level
referring phrase and an optional free-form narrative report, rather than a short class name
alone. To the best of our knowledge, RepConTUR is the first 3D referring/grounded segmentation
model to condition on such report context.
We introduce suborgan-level mask and prompt design aligned to narrative free-form radiology reports, and implement it
for abdominal tumors. • A native 3D MLLM for report-conditioned abdominal tumor segmentation. We build on prior MLLM architectures and extend them with native-3D vision modules. The MLLM vision encoder and segmentation module are all 3D,
and visual tokens are processed jointly with the report text from the first LLM layer, so vision and text are reasoned over jointly. • Report-derived multitask dataset and multitask learning. From AbdomenAtlas 3.0 [ 4 ] tumor masks and their reports we construct a unified four-task dataset. Report-matched suborgan localization produces the RES and GSEG targets, and the report is converted into radiology report generation (RRG) supervision and LLM-verified VQA pairs. We jointly train all four tasks on a single backbone. Cumulative task ablations show that report-grounded segmentation training improves RES performance, while adding report generation and VQA further increases detection F1.

term as the query (SegVol [ 19 ] , SAT [ 72 ] ,

tumor count and severity (TGANet [ 56 ] , Bi-VLGM [ 14 ] ).

blocks.en: 2.3 MLLM-based segmentation
blocks.zh: 2.3 MLLM分解

blocks.en:
This family splits into two modules. An MLLM processes text and image jointly to produce an embedding aligned to the image, and
a separate segmentation module combines that embedding with fine-grained
backbone features to produce the mask. LISA introduced this design for natural
images [ 31 ] and later works extended it [ 45 , 67 , 62 , 60 ] .
A medical branch adapts this design to biomedical images, usually in 2D. UniBioMed [ 61 ] couples an MLLM with a SAM-style segmentation module for grounded biomedical interpretation.
MedPLIB [ 28 ] drives a separate SAM-Med mask decoder from a [SEG] embedding, with the pixel-grounding path routed through an in-LLM mixture-of-experts.

blocks.en: 2.4 Multitask learning
blocks.zh: 2.4 多任务学习

blocks.en:
In the medical domain, multitask training most often pairs segmentation with a diagnostic
objective. Joint segmentation-and-classification improves segmentation over single-task
training [ 74 ] , and universal models unify detection, segmentation and diagnosis
across organs (CancerUniT [ 13 ] , CLIP-Universal [ 36 ] ). A newer
line instead couples segmentation with language tasks such as diagnostic text
generation [ 32 ] , VQA [ 28 ] and report
generation [ 22 ] . UniBioMed trains segmentation jointly with VQA and report generation
and reports improved segmentation Dice [ 61 ] .

blocks.en: 3 Report-guided multitask dataset
blocks.zh: 3 报告指导的多任务数据集

blocks.en:
We build the report-guided multitask dataset from AbdomenAtlas 3.0 [ 4 ] , which
provides 9,262 9{,}262 abdominal CT volumes with tumor masks for liver, kidney and pancreas, and organ
masks that include suborgan structures such as liver Couinaud segments. Each volume also carries a
synthetically generated radiology report from the RadGPT construction pipeline [ 4 ] .
A structured report is first derived deterministically from the masks, listing per suborgan the tumor
count, size, location, and attenuation. A large language model then rewrites the structured report
into a narrative free-text report in radiologist style. The narrative may not enumerate every tumor.

Multitask composition. We train RepConTUR jointly on four objectives, namely RES and GSEG for segmentation, RRG for radiology report generation and VQA for visual question answering.
RES conditions on a suborgan-level referring phrase drawn from a pool of phrasal variants that
indicate the tumor in a suborgan, for example “tumor in hepatic segment 7”. At training time one phrase is sampled from this pool and inserted into a randomly sampled instruction template,
such as “Please segment the tumor in {phrase}.” or “Please delineate the GTV
in {phrase}.”. RES also includes a whole-organ target that aggregates every tumor in an organ,
named by an organ-level phrase such as “total liver GTV” or “all tumors in the kidney”. GSEG reuses
the same target mask and referring phrase but prepends the full narrative report to the instruction,
such as “{report} … Based on the above findings, please segment the tumor in
{phrase}.”. The comparison therefore measures the additional benefit of report context beyond the
target phrase, with the image and requested target held fixed.

the through-slice axis, producing a 3D token grid. This encodes the whole volume in 3D at lower cost
than full 3D attention. We vary the original implementation in its input, resampling volumes to a ( 1.5 , 1.5 , 3.0 ) (1.5,1.5,3.0) mm spacing and a 240 × 240 × 140 240\times 240\times 140 grid.

pairs from Merlin [ 8 ] to generalize the encoder from chest to abdominal
radiological semantics, which our downstream abdominal tasks require. After pretraining we keep the
frozen image branch as a feature extractor.

blocks.en: 5.5 Limitations and future work
blocks.zh: 5.5 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
RepConTUR targets three abdominal organs, namely
liver, kidney and pancreas, while tumors in the other body regions are excluded in this work.
Whether the approach scales to a larger set of tumor classes, spanning further abdominal organs and
other body regions, is not established, and verifying this class-scaling ability is a primary
direction for future work.

The validation cohorts lack real reports and were grounded with synthetic ones. Although these
synthetic reports emulate the style of real narrative radiology reports, whether the same gain holds
under real clinical reports, given their stylistic variation and reporting inconsistencies, remains to
be verified. Confirming the benefit requires evaluation on datasets that pair real-world radiology
reports with their images.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We presented RepConTUR, a native-3D multimodal model that conditions abdominal tumor segmentation on a referring phrase and, optionally, a narrative report, using report-aligned suborgan masks. A report-derived dataset supports joint training on four tasks from AbdomenAtlas 3.0, namely referring and grounded segmentation, report generation and question answering. RepConTUR attains the highest DSC, precision and detection F1 among the text-promptable baselines, and improves mean detection F1 over the nnU-Net and R-Super specialists in-domain and across four external cohorts, although performance varies by organ. These results support report-conditioned segmentation under synthetic reports, and validation with independently authored clinical reports remains necessary.

blocks.en:
The four out-of-distribution cohorts ( Tab. 5 ) are built from public TCIA collections,
namely HCC-TACE-Seg [ 40 , 39 ] , Colorectal-Liver-Metastases [ 54 , 53 ] ,
CPTAC-PDA [ 42 , 49 ] and CPTAC-CCRCC [ 41 , 48 ] . The four cohorts span three organs and
both primary and metastatic disease, and each targets a distinct clinical scenario. HCC-TACE-Seg
contains primary hepatocellular carcinoma imaged in a transarterial-chemoembolization cohort, so it
probes delineation of primary liver tumors whose appearance is altered by locoregional therapy.
Colorectal-Liver-Metastases contains multifocal colorectal liver metastases, so it probes
sensitivity to several scattered deposits rather than to a single tumor. CPTAC-PDA contains
pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, an infiltrative and low-contrast primary, so it probes the hardest
abdominal target, where small tumors are the primary detection challenge. CPTAC-CCRCC contains clear
cell renal cell carcinoma and probes primary renal-tumor delineation, the organ on which the
vision-only specialist was strongest in domain.

blocks.en:
In Sec. 5.4 , the agentic inference pipeline supplies the report to RepConTUR at inference
and is compared against the vision-only nnU-Net and report-supervised R-Super specialists. This
section decomposes that comparison, evaluating each model both on its own and under the agentic
inference pipeline to isolate how much of the false-positive suppression the pipeline contributes.
Without the pipeline, RES and GSEG each run a single whole-organ pass, issuing one tumor prompt
for the entire organ rather than decomposing it into the report-named suborgans.

节分解了比较,对每个模型进行单独评估,并在剂下评估
推断输油管,以隔离输油管的虚假抑制作用有多大.

as a ratio to an even split, namely the word score divided by the mean word score of its report. The
median word lies at 0.25 × 0.25\times to 0.33 × 0.33\times across the three cases. The highest ratio in each case
falls on the tumor location, namely kidney in right kidney at 25.5 × 25.5\times with right at 9.8 × 9.8\times on the kidney case, tail at 50.2 × 50.2\times on the pancreas case, and the

reaches 14.7 × 14.7\times for hyperattenuating on the pancreas case and 7.8 × 7.8\times for hypoattenuating on the liver case, against 1.8 × 1.8\times on the kidney case. On the liver case the
count word two reaches 7.2 × 7.2\times and the size figures up to 10.6 × 10.6\times , and on the pancreas
case the size figure reaches 7.9 × 7.9\times . On the pancreas case the vessel abbreviations IVC and SMV reach 5.9 × 5.9\times and 4.4 × 4.4\times , whereas the relation words contact and encase reach 1.6 × 1.6\times and 0.5 × 0.5\times . Organ names also reach

reach high ratios, relevancy alone does not establish that a word is used.

blocks.en:
In this section we report the language tasks on the in-domain test cohort, comparing RepConTUR with the
UniBioMed baseline. For report generation UniBioMed conditions on sixteen randomly sampled 2D slices
rather than the full CT volume. We use exact-match accuracy per question type for VQA and BLEU,
ROUGE-L, METEOR [ 2 ] and BERTScore [ 69 ] for RRG. BERTScore-F1
uses DistilBERT ( distilbert-base-uncased ) following the radiology-report protocol of [ 65 ] .

the sampled 2D slices barely capture the quantitative content of these reports, namely organ volumes,
three-dimensional tumor sizes and tumor counts. In our runs the UniBioMed report head often returns
empty strings. Figure A.2 gives one qualitative example for each task.
